labels.justification: Fable B explicitly echoes the requested 'generosity quells greed' teaching in its closing line despite narrative contradictions, while Fable A muddles the identity-crisis thread and closes on only a generic friendship moral.

Both fables cut off mid-sentence before finishing, but Fable A explicitly names the 'second chance' element while Fable B better paraphrases the acceptance-brings-harmony teaching despite a confusing rumor mechanic.

Fable A wrongly sets the story in a 'flying fortress' instead of the requested floating market and never gestures at persistence, while Fable B keeps the correct setting and reads more coherently, though neither delivers the requested memorial-to-the-lost outcome.
Fable A directly states 'the prophecy has been fulfilled,' hitting the requested outcome more squarely than Fable B, though both stories end abruptly and contain garbled phrasing.

Fable B dramatizes the wise-owl-brokered compromise that matches both the showdown outcome and the wise-counsel teaching, while Fable A resolves the conflict off-screen via unexplained new characters and never delivers a real showdown.
